tagline: Up an emigrant ridge to Carson Pass, and quickly down.
intro: Highway 88 climbs the western slope of the Sierra Nevada on a ridge, where it joins the Mormon Emigrant Trail, with overlooks into the river canyons on either side. Past Silver Lake it reaches the Carson Spur, and the ridge gives out. The road drops on a dynamited path to Kirkwood, then climbs past Caples Lake to Carson Pass.

The east side comes down fast, past a view of Red Lake, into Hope Valley at about 7,000 feet under peaks above 10,000, and out through Woodfords Canyon. Caltrans tries to keep this pass open all year. Every other Sierra pass from here south to Walker Pass closes for winter.
season: Autumn: Hope Valley and Woodfords Canyon are often cited among the best areas in California for fall foliage.

moments.title: Kirkwood
moments.text: Zack Kirkwood opened his inn here in 1863. The county lines have moved since, but the old signpost where three counties met is still inside the building.

moments.title: Carson Pass
moments.text: Mormons leaving California for Utah built a wagon trail over this pass in 1848. Kit Carson carved his name into a tree at the summit, and the Pacific Crest Trail crosses here.

moments.title: Woodfords
moments.text: In April 1860 Warren Upson rode down out of a snowstorm and made this a Pony Express remount station. Five weeks later the Express went another way.

practical: The Carson Spur, east of Silver Lake, is prone to avalanches and is closed from time to time in winter for avalanche control.
